question: On the consumed RoMa cohort, does temporally local active-frame selection repair true-pair recall without changing the dense matcher or absolute-support rule?

predecessor.failure_signature: Minimum-baseline-first selection could choose temporally distant revisits, including a 525-frame gap, despite a 0.30 m camera-centre separation.
predecessor.single_change: Rank qualifying frame pairs by minimum frame gap before baseline and visibility; keep all model, crop, certainty, cycle, support, assignment, scenario and gate values unchanged.

provider.name: SceneNN
provider.sensor: Asus Xtion PRO consumer RGB-D camera
provider.license_boundary: Educational and research use; raw SceneNN payloads remain local and are not redistributed.

pre_rgb_selector.pair_ranking: minimum qualifying frame gap, then minimum qualifying camera-centre baseline, maximum minimum visible target pixels, maximum minimum visibility ratio, earlier frames

renderer.near_plane_face_rule: reject unless every vertex is beyond near plane
renderer.visibility_rule: target depth finite and no farther than full-scene depth plus 0.005 m

pre_rgb_selector.failure_semantics: If any consumed target lacks a qualifying temporally local pair, stop NOT_EVALUABLE without changing the rules.

matcher.absolute_support: unchanged bilateral one-percent cycle fraction and majority cycle purity
matcher.rank_score: unchanged geometric mean of directional cycle-consistent fractions
matcher.zero_assignment: unchanged strict reciprocal maximum among supported pairs

forbidden_after_rgb_access: change frame ranking, scenes, targets, crop, model, resolution, certainty threshold, cycle tolerance, support fractions, assignment, scenarios or gate
